title: Yields Scream Higher, Gold And Silver At Pivot Break Point: $3,500 And $50 Odds Increase!
speaker: Gareth Soloway

macro_themes.view: 10-year yields near 5.35%, highest since 2002, rising on strong economy rather than inflation.
US stocks shrug off high yields and oil as global money seeks US safety; issues expected in 2027.
Rising yields threaten gold and silver trendline breakdowns, but long-term bullish on hard assets.

calls.condition: if it closes above the 2007 peak, especially with confirmation, expects 5.5%
calls.reason: Yields recovered after weak jobs and are above the 2007 peak, highest since 2002, driven by strong economy, debt and global unrest.
calls.quote: if we close above this level, especially with confirmation, I would insinuate or expect a move up to the 5.5% level on yields.

calls.condition: above ~7575 stays net long; 7400-7575 neutral zone; below ~7400 out of longs and heavily short
calls.reason: Most resilient market in a while: strong earnings ahead, global money seeking US safety, strong economy; trendline target near 8,000 through the midterms into year-end before issues in 2027.
calls.quote: it is bullish and expecting upside with a target of this.

calls.condition: break of the trendline at ~4100 targets 3950-3960; break of 3950 targets 3500; would buy at 3500
calls.reason: Gold bear-flagging on a trendline from May 2025 while yields rise; scene-of-the-crime breakout revisit possible. Long-term bull on fiscal irresponsibility.
calls.quote: If it breaks 3950, which was the previous low on the last dip, it is going down to 3500.

calls.condition: if silver breaks its long-term trendline, support at 54-55, then likely just below 50
calls.reason: Silver sitting on a longer-term trendline; relatively stronger than gold on strong economic data; target is the 1980/2011 high just below 50.
calls.quote: If it breaks that, you're likely headed down to this pivot just below 50.

notes: Speaks of 'today' after Friday's jobs report and morning ISM services; listing date (Monday) used.
